title: Know Your Rights: Constitution Quiz
theme: Indian Constitution, Fundamental Rights & Civic Duties
description: How well do you know your rights? 20 rapid-fire questions about the Indian Constitution, fundamental rights, directive principles, fundamental duties, and how our democracy works. Every citizen should know these -- test yourself!
reflection_prompt: Which right or duty surprised you the most, and how might knowing it change something you do as a citizen?
learning_objectives: Understand the structure of the Indian Constitution
Learn about Fundamental Rights (Part III) and Duties (Part IV-A)
Know key constitutional amendments and their significance
Understand the roles of Parliament, Judiciary, and Executive

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each scenario-based question about the Indian Constitution, fundamental rights, duties, or government structure
Select your answer before the 15-second timer runs out
Earn 10 points per correct answer, plus streak bonuses for consecutive correct answers
Work through all 20 questions covering the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Duties, Directive Principles, amendments, and government structure
Review your results to discover how well you know your constitutional rights and duties as an Indian citizen
tips: Read the full scenario carefully -- many questions describe real-life situations that hint at the correct Article or provision
Build answer streaks for extra points -- each consecutive correct answer earns a 5-point bonus
Remember that Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Articles 12-35) and Fundamental Duties are in Article 51A
If unsure, eliminate the most obviously wrong options first to improve your chances

questions.question: Priya's school refuses her admission solely because she belongs to a Scheduled Caste. Which Fundamental Right protects her against this discrimination?
questions.correct_answer: Right to Equality (Article 15)

questions.question: Rahul, a 13-year-old, is forced to work in a firecracker factory for 12 hours a day. Which Article of the Constitution specifically prohibits the employment of children below 14 in hazardous jobs?
options: Article 24 -- Prohibition of Child Labour in Factories
questions.correct_answer: Article 24 -- Prohibition of Child Labour in Factories

questions.question: Meera wants to start a student newspaper at her school to discuss social issues. Which Fundamental Right guarantees her the freedom of speech and expression?
options: Article 19(1)(a) -- Freedom of Speech and Expression
questions.correct_answer: Article 19(1)(a) -- Freedom of Speech and Expression

questions.question: Arjun is wrongfully detained by police without being told the reason for his arrest. He wants to challenge this in court. Which Article is called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution because it allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly to enforce their Fundamental Rights?
options: Article 21 -- Right to Life and Personal Liberty
questions.correct_answer: Article 32 -- Right to Constitutional Remedies

questions.question: A private company pays different salaries to male and female employees doing the exact same job. Which constitutional provision guarantees equal pay for equal work?
options: Article 39(d) -- Directive Principle: Equal Pay for Equal Work
Article 16 -- Equality of Opportunity in Public Employment
questions.correct_answer: Article 39(d) -- Directive Principle: Equal Pay for Equal Work

questions.question: Kavya, a minority community student, wants to attend a school run by her religious community that teaches both regular subjects and her community's language and culture. Which Article protects the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions?
options: Article 25 -- Freedom of Conscience and Religion
Article 29 -- Protection of Interests of Minorities
Article 30 -- Right of Minorities to Establish Educational Institutions
Article 28 -- Freedom from Religious Instruction in State-funded Institutions
questions.correct_answer: Article 30 -- Right of Minorities to Establish Educational Institutions

questions.question: Which word was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, reflecting India's commitment to an economy with both public and private sector participation?
questions.correct_answer: Socialist

questions.question: The Preamble declares India to be a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic.' What does 'Secular' mean in the Indian context?
options: India has no official state religion and treats all religions equally
India follows only Hindu traditions in governance
Religion is banned in public life
Only majority religions are recognized by the state
questions.correct_answer: India has no official state religion and treats all religions equally

questions.question: Vikram's village has no proper roads, clean water, or primary health centre. The state government argues it has no legal obligation to provide these. Which part of the Constitution contains guiding principles for the state to ensure social and economic welfare, even though they are not enforceable in court?
options: Part IV -- Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.correct_answer: Part IV -- Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.question: During a classroom debate, Ananya says that it is every citizen's duty to protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India. She is referring to which part of the Constitution?
questions.correct_answer: Fundamental Duties under Article 51A (Part IV-A)

questions.question: Rohan sees his classmates littering in a public park and vandalising a heritage monument. He reminds them that the Constitution lists specific duties for citizens. Which Fundamental Duty calls on citizens to protect public property and to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture?
options: Duty to defend the country and render national service
Duty to safeguard public property and abjure violence
Duty to develop a scientific temper and humanism
Duty to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
questions.correct_answer: Duty to safeguard public property and abjure violence

questions.question: Sneha's teacher asks: 'Which Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, making it a duty of parents and guardians regarding children aged 6 to 14?' What is the correct answer?
options: Duty to vote in every election
Duty to provide opportunities for education to their child
Duty to pay taxes on time
questions.correct_answer: Duty to provide opportunities for education to their child

questions.question: India's Parliament consists of two houses. Which of the following correctly names both houses?
options: Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States)
questions.correct_answer: Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States)

questions.question: Amit reads in the newspaper that a new law passed by Parliament has been struck down by the Supreme Court for violating Fundamental Rights. This power of the judiciary to declare laws unconstitutional is known as:
questions.correct_answer: Judicial Review

questions.question: The President of India is the constitutional head of state. Who elects the President?
options: Directly by the citizens of India through universal adult suffrage
By the members of both Houses of Parliament only
By an Electoral College consisting of elected members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies
By the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers
questions.correct_answer: By an Electoral College consisting of elected members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies

questions.question: In a civics class discussion, the teacher asks: 'Who is the real executive authority in India's parliamentary system -- the one who actually runs the government?' What is the correct answer?
options: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers
questions.correct_answer: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers

questions.question: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is often called the 'Mini-Constitution' because of the sweeping changes it introduced. Which of the following was a key addition made by this amendment?
options: It added Fundamental Duties to the Constitution and inserted the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' in the Preamble
It introduced the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right
It created the Supreme Court of India
questions.correct_answer: It added Fundamental Duties to the Constitution and inserted the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' in the Preamble

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) was a landmark for grassroots democracy in India. What did it establish?
options: Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions (local self-government in rural areas)
questions.correct_answer: Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions (local self-government in rural areas)

questions.question: Deepa, aged 7, is not going to school because her parents cannot afford it. The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A to the Constitution. What right does this Article guarantee?
options: Right to free healthcare for all children
Right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
Right to free meals in government schools
Right to vocational training for teenagers
questions.correct_answer: Right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years

questions.question: A person is illegally detained by authorities and their family files a petition in the High Court demanding that the detained person be produced before the court. Which type of writ are they most likely filing?
options: Mandamus -- commanding a public authority to perform its duty
Habeas Corpus -- produce the body of the detained person before the court
Certiorari -- quashing the order of a lower court
Quo Warranto -- questioning the authority of a person holding public office
questions.correct_answer: Habeas Corpus -- produce the body of the detained person before the court

glossary_terms.definition: The introductory statement of the Indian Constitution that declares India to be a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic. It outlines the objectives of the Constitution -- justice (social, economic, and political), liberty, equality, and fraternity. Often called the 'identity card' of the Constitution, it was inspired by the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946.

A set of rights guaranteed to all citizens under Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution. These include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and the Right to Constitutional Remedies. They are enforceable by courts and can be claimed against the state.

A formal written order issued by the Supreme Court (under Article 32) or a High Court (under Article 226) to enforce Fundamental Rights or correct a legal wrong. The five types of writs are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto. Filing a writ petition is the primary mechanism for citizens to seek judicial protection of their constitutional rights.

A Latin term meaning 'produce the body.' It is one of the five constitutional writs that can be issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts. When a person is unlawfully detained or imprisoned, a Habeas Corpus petition requires the detaining authority to present the detained person before the court and justify the detention. It is considered the most powerful safeguard of personal liberty.

The power of the Supreme Court and High Courts to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts (laws passed by Parliament or state legislatures) and executive orders. If a law or action is found to violate the Constitution -- especially Fundamental Rights -- the judiciary can declare it null and void. This power is derived from Articles 13, 32, and 226 and is a key feature of the basic structure doctrine established in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).
